## Why This Is Asked

Tests ability to translate CKNE scores into concrete ingestion controls (backpressure, queues, durability) in a shared data lake. Also checks how to implement time-based degradation with fairness and observability.

## Key Concepts

- CKNE-to-backpressure mapping for per-tenant tokens and partitions
- Durable queues and at-least-once guarantees under throttling
- Minute-by-minute degradation loop and fair redistribution

## Code Example

```javascript
// Pseudo admission check sketch
function canAccept(tenant, ckne, tokens, partitions) {
  const t = tokens[tenant] ?? 0
  const p = partitions[tenant] ?? 0
  if (ckne >= 0.6) return t > 0 && p > 0
  // throttle aggressively for ckne < 0.4
  return t > 0 && p > 0 && (ckne > 0.2 || t > 1)
}
```

## Follow-up Questions

- How to validate fairness under burst CKNE shifts?
- How would regional replicas affect backpressure signals?

## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to design CKNE-driven multi-region data strategies, balancing latency, residency, and fairness under real-world failures.

## Key Concepts
- CKNE-to-replica mapping across regions
- Cross-region latency budgets and data residency SLAs
- Minimal disruption during rebalancing
- Failure/invalidation handling and auditability

## Code Example
```javascript
function replicaTargets(ckne, regions, base=1){
  const total = Math.max(1, Math.round(ckne * regions.length * base));
  const perRegion = Math.max(1, Math.floor(total / regions.length));
  return regions.reduce((acc,r)=>({...acc,[r]: perRegion}), {});
}
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How do you detect oscillation in replica counts and dampen it?
- How would you extend for tenants entering/leaving the CKNE spectrum?
